content:
sasha: FYI customer ACME-prod is seeing a sudden throughput drop on dedicated pool d-pool-12. Lots of 429s and tail latency up. Filing here for triage.

ops-bot: ALERT: d-pool-12 throttle spike detected (15:22 UTC) — 3m elevated 429 rate.

jenna: Thanks. Do we have request_ids or traces? Customer ticket says "all requests slow" and some 429s.

sasha: Ticket https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/CS-3421, example request_id: req_0b9f2c. Attached logs:
```
2026-02-18T15:21:43Z INFO pool=d-pool-12 req=req_0b9f2c status=429 reason=throttle batch_size=2 tokens=24 latency_ms=320
2026-02-18T15:21:44Z INFO pool=d-pool-12 req=req_0b9f2d status=200 batch_size=1 tokens=8 latency_ms=900
2026-02-18T15:21:45Z INFO pool=d-pool-12 req=req_0b9f2e status=200 batch_size=1 tokens=6 latency_ms=780
metrics: avg_batch_size=1.3 median=1 p95_batch_size=2
```

kai: That avg_batch_size is tiny. Could be packing/scheduler mis-sorting or the continuous batcher prefill threshold is too aggressive causing many thin windows. Also autoscale not triggering? Any recent quota or autoscaler events?

marco: Autoscale logs for the timeline show scale decisions but no new nodes added because pool reached max_reserved=4. Customer on small dedicated tier. So autoscale didn't add capacity due to cap.

jenna: Confirmed customer on reserved=4. They expected burst to 8 but config cap=4 in DC. Eng-sre may need to help or offer short-term bump.

kai: Hypothesis: small-window starvation — many short requests (6–24 tokens) are arriving spread out, scheduler forming windows that prefer low-latency and flush early, producing many 1-2 sized batches. With max_batch_tokens low (1024) that's fine, but continuous batcher window_ms maybe set to 10ms which flushes too quickly under our arrival pattern. Also fair-queueing may be prioritizing by tenant arrival causing noisy-tenant effect.

sasha: Repro steps I used: hit the pool with 50 concurrent short prompts (~10 tokens) at 200rps from our perf worker in us-west2. Attached quick curl:
```bash
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer ${TOKEN}" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"rwd-30b", "input":"Q: Hi\nA:"}' &
done
wait
```
observed: most responses had batch_size<=2, p95 latency up ~700ms, some 429s.

support-bot: note: customer billing unaffected, but they hit service-level pain. CS asked for ETA on mitigation.

marco: Quick mitigations: (1) bump customer pool max_reserved temporarily to 8 (operational), (2) change continuous_batcher.window_ms from 10 -> 30 for that pool, (3) increase scheduler.packetization to prefer token-packing vs arrival-time. We'll test (2) first on a canary host.

kai: I'll run a local canary: change config snippet below and watch batch_size metrics and 429 rate.
```yaml
pool: d-pool-12
continuous_batcher:
  window_ms: 30
  prefill_threshold: 0.6
scheduler:
  pack_by: "tokens"
  max_batch_tokens: 4096
```

kai: Expected outcome: larger avg_batch_size (closer to 8–12), reduced per-token latency and fewer 429s because we use capacity more efficiently. If packing works, we may not need to bump reserved nodes.

jenna: CS wants us to confirm within 1 hour or do the reserved bump. Marco — can ops do temp bump if needed?

marco: Ops can do immediate bump to 6 (not full 8) while we canary. I'll schedule change at 15:40 UTC if canary looks OK.

sasha: Canary run at 15:30 UTC with window_ms=30 — metrics so far: avg_batch_size jumped to 6.1, p95 latency down to 230ms, 429s dropped to baseline.

kai: Good sign. I'll roll pool-wide config on a 10% canary then 50% if stable. Also filing follow-up: we should add a scheduler metric that shows token-packing efficiency per tenant to catch regression.

jenna: Noted — CS updated customer with temporary bump plan + ETA to revert if stable.

sasha: Action items: kai -> rollout config canary & monitor (assigned). marco -> hold temporary reserved bump ready + rollback plan. jenna -> update CS and include repro steps. I'll paste the perf job and traces to the ticket.

support-bot: Triage complete. Closing slack loop; follow-ups in CS-3421 and ENG-4567. :thumbsup:
